content: This chapter focuses on the development and implementation of national programs aimed at improving adolescent health and well-being. It outlines pathways for designing programs that address adolescent well-being, strategies for multisectoral collaboration, and key implementation approaches for both intersectoral and single-sector actions across critical areas such as health, education, social protection, criminal justice, labor, telecommunications, transportation, housing, urban planning, energy, and the environment. The second edition of the Global Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) guidance builds on the systematic approach of the first edition but now incorporates enhanced, evidence-based support for multisectoral action. This updated edition aims to deepen the understanding of the relationship between adolescent health, well-being, and their determinants. It includes new data on global adolescent populations, mortality, morbidity, health outcomes, risk and protective factors, and determinants of health and well-being. Since the first edition in 2017, significant political and scientific advancements have occurred. These include the launch of major global initiatives, new research insights, updated guidelines, and resources supporting universal health coverage (UHC). These advancements emphasize quality care, provider competencies, advocacy for investment in adolescent health, and balancing specific programs with overall system strengthening. The second edition integrates lessons learned from the application of the first edition, including new case studies and updated reference documents. The concept of adolescent well-being has evolved, with a consensus framework developed by UN H6+ agencies and the Partnership for Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (PMNCH). This framework defines adolescent well-being as the state in which adolescents have the support, confidence, and resources to thrive in secure and healthy relationships, realizing their full potential and rights. The second edition shifts from a health-centric perspective to a more holistic understanding of adolescent well-being, incorporating its implications for program design. Lessons from the pandemic are integrated into the guidance to build resilient educational and other systems critical to adolescent health and well-being. The second edition was developed through extensive collaboration with WHO departments, regional and country offices, UN organizations, PMNCH, and global partners. It involved eight multi-stakeholder consultations with member states across all six WHO regions in 2021. A technical working group, including young people and representatives from various organizations, directed the process by mapping new evidence, initiatives, and programmatic experiences. A global public consultation in 2023 further refined the document, incorporating inputs from end users and young people. Adolescents and young people emphasized the importance of prioritizing mental health, access to healthcare, meaningful youth engagement, and addressing social determinants of health such as poverty, gender inequality, and discrimination. They also highlighted the need for free or affordable healthcare and the inclusion of topics related to sexual and reproductive health. The guidance underscores adolescence as a critical phase of human development, requiring dedicated attention in national policies and programs. Investments in adolescent well-being yield a triple dividend of benefits: immediate health and economic gains, improved outcomes in adulthood, and positive impacts on the next generation. These investments are essential for achieving the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, addressing goals related to poverty, education, gender equality, and more. The COVID-19 pandemic has reinforced the importance of global health investments and the role of schools in providing not only education but also critical services such as nutrition, mental health support, and social protection. This presents a unique opportunity to reinvigorate global commitments to adolescent health and well-being. The AA-HA. guidance has been instrumental in accelerating action on adolescent health and well-being since its launch in 2017. Many countries have used it to develop or update comprehensive strategies and plans. The guidance has also informed regional initiatives and political commitments, demonstrating its adaptability to diverse contexts. It emphasizes involving adolescents in planning processes, fostering multisectoral collaboration, and providing detailed, practical tools for implementation. The second edition incorporates lessons learned from the first edition, advances a positive vision of health that integrates physical, mental, spiritual, and social well-being, and promotes a focus on adolescent well-being within UHC targets. It highlights the importance of school health, with initiatives such as Making Every School a Health-Promoting School and the Global School Meals Coalition. The guidance also addresses contemporary threats to adolescent health, such as climate change, armed conflicts, and displacement. In summary, the second edition of the AA-HA. guidance provides a comprehensive framework for advancing adolescent health and well-being, integrating new evidence, lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, and a holistic understanding of well-being. It emphasizes the importance of multisectoral collaboration, meaningful youth engagement, and investments in adolescent health as essential for achieving sustainable development goals and building a healthier, more equitable future.
